1.why: Source P1: scramble mostly class 4 to a belay ledge with a large dead tree
1.text: The first belay is on a ledge where a large dead tree stands, reached after the fourth-class scramble.

2.why: Source P2 ends at an obvious belay bench with a south-face rappel anchor; 'flat' unsupported, removed
2.text: The second belay is on an obvious bench at the top of the blocky pitch, with a rappel anchor there for the south face.

1.why: Squamish guide P1: belay stance just below left-slanting twin cracks
1.text: Belay on a stance directly below the pair of left-slanting twin cracks.

4.why: Squamish guide P4 ends on to the Supercave past the second bolt; cave-floor detail trimmed
4.text: The belay is in the Supercave, just past the hard step-up beyond the second bolt.

5.why: Squamish guide P5 ends at a pedestal belay ledge after the left-side exit and corner
5.text: The belay is a pedestal-style ledge reached after leaving the cave on its left side and following the corner.

7.why: Second page: P7 5.8 optional 15m face pitch to a tree; 'top of the wall' trimmed
7.text: The last belay is at a tree reached by a short optional 5.8 face pitch.

3.why: Trip report: 5.4 past pitons then back left to a small alcove below a chimney; two pitons and a chock stone as anchors
3.text: Belay in a small alcove at the foot of a chimney, anchored to fixed pitons and a wedged chockstone.
